name: Quantifier Granularity Profile
description: Analyzes the statistical distribution and specificity of quantifier words (e.g., 'many', 'some', 'few', 'all', 'several', 'most'). Large Language Models exhibit a strong algorithmic preference for vague, non-committal quantifiers ('many experts agree', 'some studies suggest') over precise numerical data or risky absolute claims ('all experts', 'none'). This behavior stems from perplexity optimization and safety guardrails designed to prevent the model from generating hallucinated specifics or easily falsifiable absolute statements.
algorithm: Fuzzy vs. Absolute Quantifier Ratio Extraction
mechanism: The analyzer extracts all quantity-indicating terms and categorizes them into two bins: 'Fuzzy Quantifiers' (some, many, various) and 'Absolute/Precise Quantifiers' (all, zero, exact numbers). It calculates the ratio between these two sets. Because AI models are fundamentally probability engines tuned (via RLHF) to avoid generating false absolutes, they mathematically cluster their outputs around safe, fuzzy quantifiers. A human writer typically anchors arguments with precise data or uses absolutes for rhetorical effect. The system flags texts that maintain a suspiciously high, unvarying density of vague quantifiers without committing to specific values.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing research summaries, market analyses, and academic essays where a machine will lean heavily on phrases like 'various factors' or 'many cases' rather than citing specific figures like human domain experts.
strengths:
• Excellent at exposing AI 'hallucination avoidance' tactics, where the model masks a lack of specific retrieved data behind broad quantifiers.
• Highly persistent across different language models, as generic quantification is a core feature of base probability generation.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in sociological or speculative writing where broad generalizations are contextually appropriate.
• Easily disrupted if a human user heavily prompts the AI to inject fake, specific numerical values into the text.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical Extraction and Specificity Categorization
Metric: Fuzzy-to-Absolute Quantifier Ratio
Output: 0-100 Vague Quantification (Artificial Generality) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 70-80% standalone accuracy. It is highly context-dependent and should be combined with Lexical Specificity and Evidence Citation analysis.
